title: EKS: Kubernetes control plane does not operate your application
outcome: Choose EKS for a concrete Kubernetes need and map AWS responsibility versus cluster/workload responsibility.
useCase: Teams with a justified Kubernetes platform need.
benefits: Managed Kubernetes integration and ecosystem access.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: Managed control plane. Deliberately operated workload.

trace.title: EKS responsibility map
trace.detail: EKS supplies managed Kubernetes offerings. You still need to understand the selected mode’s responsibilities: workload configuration, identity, networking, storage, admission/access, observability, upgrades, and application recovery.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Manifest desired state → API admission → controller reconciliation → scheduler/capacity → pod process → readiness → service traffic. Then trace a pod reschedule and a rollout with the DB unchanged.

Map every secret, network permission, and persistent data store to its owner. A healthy control plane does not prove your app is healthy.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Running a DB in a StatefulSet does not create a complete backup/HA plan. A broad node role can accidentally become every pod’s effective access. More platform components can increase incident surface.
